title: Proportional Threshold Allocator with Policy Shields
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Dedicated capacity customers require firm throughput guarantees while allowing safe automated scaling during demand variation. Current autoscaler prototypes handle percentile-based targets but struggle with mixed workloads (short streaming requests + long context completions) and tenant burst isolation. This ticket designs and implements a Proportional Threshold Allocator (PTA) that composes multiple target metrics (p50/p95 token latency, tail concurrency, per-tenant TPS) and enforces policy "shields" (safety caps, surge windows, budgeted headroom) to prevent oscillation or cost-explosive behavior.

Goals:
- Define a multi-metric target expression language for autoscale policies that combines latency percentiles, effective throughput, and queue depth.
- Implement scaling algorithms: proportional-integral (PI)-inspired stepper with hysteresis, a conservative quantized grow/shrink mode, and an emergency fallback that pins to committed capacity.
- Add safety shields: temporal rate limits for scale-up, decay-based headroom credits for burst absorbtion, and per-tenant fail-open/closed policies that map to dedicated vs shared pools.
- Provide observability hooks and SLO-aligned traces so operators can audit scale decisions and simulate policy effects in staging.

Non-goals: full ML-driven autoscaler, cross-region rebalancing, pricing changes.

Design notes:
- Target expression: policies are authored as weighted composites. Example: scale_target = 0.6*latency_p95_scale + 0.3*throughput_scale + 0.1*concurrency_scale. Each term normalizes to a unitless scale factor relative to current capacity.
- Proportional Threshold Allocator (PTA): computes desired_capacity = max(min_capacity, ceil(current_capacity * composite_scale * smoothing_factor)). The smoothing_factor is derived from a PI-like accumulator but capped by policy shields.
- Hysteresis and step limits: enforce min_time_between_events, max_percent_change_per_action, and separate step limits for scaling up vs down.
- Headroom credits: when traffic surges, consume credits to allow temporary oversubscription; credits replenish slowly during steady-state underutilization.
- Emergency fallback: if error rates or model OOMs spike, immediately trigger a policy-defined fallback that reduces concurrency targets and routes to lower-cost model variants or enqueues requests.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/pta-design-2025
- Simulation harness (internal GH): https://github.com/redwood-inference/auto-sim/pull/312
- Early perf dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/dedicated/autoscale-pta-staging

Risks & trade-offs:
- More sophisticated composite targets increase policy complexity for customers; include sensible defaults and a policy linter.
- Headroom credits can mask underprovisioning; add budget exhaustion alerts and opt-out flags.
- Rapid policy changes require safe rollout — implement canary policies and an immediate rollback hook.

Implementation plan:
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize target expression spec, add CI policy linter, and author three canonical policy templates (latency-first, throughput-first, balanced).
Week 2: Implement PTA core algorithm in autoscaler service (compute composite_scale, smoothing, step caps).
Week 3: Add policy shields (headroom credits store, rate-limited scale-up, emergency fallback).
Week 4: Integrate tracing & dashboard metrics; run simulation harness with synthetic mixed workloads.
Week 5: Staging rollout to a small set of Dedicated fleets; collect regressions and iterate.
acceptance_criteria: Policy language supports combining at least latency_p50, latency_p95, effective_tps, and queue_depth into a single composite target.
Autoscaler produces deterministic, explainable scale actions in staging that match simulator predictions > 90% of the time.
Safety shields prevent >40% capacity growth within a 5-minute window unless promoted by an explicit emergency policy.
Headroom credits allow short bursts (up to configured budget) without violating latency SLOs for at least 99% of requests.
Observability: each scale decision emits a trace with inputs (metrics), composite score breakdown, shield triggers, and resulting action ID.
Canary policy rollout demonstrates safe rollback path and no customer-facing errors for a 24h validation window.
